rationale: A2.8B requires technology regression to write linear, quadratic, and exponential functions. Fidelity V2 uses fit-only secure Data Modeling Lab modes so prediction is not imported from A2.8C, uses overdetermined noisy data, requires every fitted coefficient, and includes growth, decay, and full transcription repair.

documents.prompt: Use linear regression technology on all five observations, $(-2,{{ym2}})$, $(-1,{{ym1}})$, $(0,{{y0}})$, $(1,{{y1}})$, and $(2,{{y2}})$, to write the line of best fit $y=mx+b$. Enter the regression slope and intercept reported by the technology.

context.title: Noisy linear data
context.note: The five points do not lie perfectly on one line. Use regression on the complete data set rather than choosing two convenient points.

solutionReview.headline: Regression uses all observations, including the residual variation.
reasoning: The residual pattern is balanced around the generating line, so the full least-squares regression recovers m={{m}} and b={{b}}.
A line through only two selected points can give a different result; the standard requires regression technology on the data set.

attemptFeedback: Run linear regression on all five rows; do not calculate slope from only two points.
supportHints: Enter both regression outputs m and b exactly as technology reports them.

variants.prompt: Use linear regression technology on all five observations, $(-2,{{ym2}})$, $(-1,{{ym1}})$, $(0,{{y0}})$, $(1,{{y1}})$, and $(2,{{y2}})$, to write the line of best fit $y=mx+b$. The coefficients and noise are intentionally small; enter the fitted slope and intercept reported by the technology.

documents.prompt: Use quadratic regression technology on the complete five-row data set, $(-2,{{ym2}})$, $(-1,{{ym1}})$, $(0,{{y0}})$, $(1,{{y1}})$, and $(2,{{y2}})$, to write $y=ax^2+bx+c$. Enter all three fitted coefficients.

context.title: Noisy quadratic data
context.note: The observations include small residual variation, so fitting only three points is not equivalent to running quadratic regression.

solutionReview.headline: Quadratic regression uses all five observations to estimate three coefficients.
reasoning: The balanced residual pattern is orthogonal to the constant, x, and x² columns used by least squares.
Therefore the full regression recovers a={{a}}, b={{b}}, and c={{c}} even though no five-row perfect parabola is shown.

attemptFeedback: Use quadratic regression on the complete list and record a, b, and c.
supportHints: Do not hand-fit three selected points; the extra observations are part of the regression evidence.

documents.prompt: {{scenario}} Use exponential regression technology on all five positive observations to write the fitted function $y=a(b)^x$. Enter the fitted initial factor a and base b.

context.title: Noisy exponential growth data
context.note: The points vary slightly above and below a perfect exponential curve. Use exponential regression rather than consecutive-ratio recognition.

solutionReview.headline: Exponential regression linearizes the positive outputs on a logarithmic scale.
reasoning: The multiplicative noise is balanced on the log scale, so technology recovers the underlying fitted initial factor and growth base.
The fitted base is greater than 1, which is consistent with exponential growth.
solutionReview.answerSummary: Record the technology's fitted a and growth base b.

attemptFeedback: Use exponential regression on the full list; the raw consecutive ratios are intentionally not constant.
supportHints: Both a and b must come from the regression output.

documents.prompt: {{scenario}} The quantity is decaying, but the measurements are not perfectly exponential. Use exponential regression technology on all five observations to write the fitted function $y=a(b)^x$. Enter a and b.

context.title: Measured exponential decay
context.note: Measurement variation makes consecutive ratios unequal. The fitted base should come from regression technology, not from one chosen pair.

solutionReview.headline: Regression distinguishes an overall exponential decay pattern from small measurement variation.
reasoning: The fitted base is between 0 and 1, so the fitted model represents decay.
All five positive observations contribute to the technology estimate.
solutionReview.answerSummary: Record the technology's fitted a and decay base b.

attemptFeedback: Do not average two ratios by hand; use the exponential regression command on all five observations.
supportHints: A valid decay fit has a positive initial factor and a base between 0 and 1.

documents.prompt: A student runs quadratic regression on the five observations but records the x-term coefficient with the opposite sign, writing $y={{a}}x^2+({{wrongB}})x+({{c}})$. Re-run quadratic regression on the full data set and repair the complete fitted function by entering the actual a, b, and c.

context.title: Repair a regression transcription error
context.note: The displayed student equation is not an answer key. Verify every coefficient against a fresh technology regression on all five observations.

solutionReview.headline: Regression output must be transcribed faithfully before the model is used.
reasoning: The student's x-term sign disagrees with the regression output.
Re-running the five-row quadratic regression gives a={{a}}, b={{b}}, c={{c}}.
The corrected fitted function uses b={{b}}, not {{wrongB}}.

attemptFeedback: Re-run the regression rather than changing only the displayed sign by assumption.
supportHints: Compare all three coefficients from technology with the student's recorded model.

variants.prompt: A student runs quadratic regression on five observations but copies the x-term coefficient with the wrong sign. Re-run the regression, identify the transcription error, and enter the correct a, b, and c.
